details:
Alaz (AETHER-FIRE) is an independent research prototype for comparing NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspot observations from MODIS and VIIRS. Changes in sensor footprints, confidence classes, or satellite coverage can look like changes in fire activity, making long-term records difficult to interpret. Alaz keeps raw detections visible alongside a harmonized VIIRS-equivalent estimate, using a documented confidence policy and a biome-stratified model trained on physically simulated MODIS–VIIRS matchups.

The app combines a global recent-data view with a historical archive pilot for Turkey. Users can select a region of interest, examine sensor and platform breakdowns, explore time series, burning calendars, anomalies and diagnostics around the 2012 sensor transition, and export hotspot records or generate a caveated briefing. The interface is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Python, FastAPI, H3 and Chart.js, with Mapbox GL and an OpenStreetMap fallback.

Alaz is designed to make assumptions and data limitations visible. Synthetic benchmark results are kept separate from real-archive comparisons; VIIRS is treated as a reference, not ground truth. Independent event-level validation remains future work. Alaz supports research and pre-screening, not fire prediction or operational dispatch.
